newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SARFU POSTPONES DRUGS HEARING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SARFU POSTPONES DRUGS HEARING.

text.p: The South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) postponed indefinitely a drugs hearing into three players on Tuesday because of fears the proceedings could have been unconstitutional.

SARFU chief executive Rian Oberholzer said in a statement that SARFU's regulations, which did not allow for legal representation at disciplinary hearings, could be in conflict with the new constitution.
"We have become aware that this section of our regulations may be in conflict with the new constitution of South Africa. For this reason, we have decided to postpone the hearings.
"The issues of illegal drugs being used in South African rugby and of bringing the game into disrepute are issues that SARFU treats with the utmost seriousness.
"We would like to have these issues settled as quickly as possible."
But Oberholzer said the constitutional issue had to be resolved before the hearings could take place.

None of the three rugby players who tested positive for illegal substances has yet been officially named by SARFU but Springbok lock Johan Ackerman is known to have tested positive in January and has not played for Northern Transvaal in the ongoing Super 12 series.
